name: legacy-elements
note: Deprecated HTML elements get no UA styling by design (modern-compat legacy-removal policy, docs/ledgers/legacy-removal.md). The engine renders center/tt/dir/menu/font/big/strike as generic block boxes; Chrome still applies its UA stylesheet (center text-align center, tt inline+monospace, dir/menu 40px list padding, big inline+larger, strike inline+line-through), so every layer intentionally diverges and is declared as a typed gap. The verify script separately asserts the engine-side generic-box contract.

harvest.html: <style>html,body{margin:0;padding:0}</style><center id="c">centered text</center><tt id="tt">teletype</tt><dir id="dir">dir text</dir><menu id="menu">menu text</menu><font id="font">font text</font><big id="big">big text</big><strike id="strike">strike text</strike>

computedStyle.reason: Engine renders deprecated elements as generic block boxes (center text-align start, tt display block + no monospace, dir/menu padding-left 0px, font/big/strike display block) while Chrome still applies its UA stylesheet (center text-align center, tt inline+monospace, dir/menu 40px padding, big inline+larger, strike inline+line-through). Intentional by design per the modern-compat policy.
computedStyle.sunset: Permanent by design — legacy elements are never styled again; retire only if the policy is reversed and Chrome's legacy UA defaults are reproduced.

rect.reason: Legacy elements stack as 400px-wide generic block boxes in the engine (one per line) while Chrome flows tt/font/big/strike inline and gives dir/menu 40px padding, so every id's border box diverges. Intentional by design.
rect.sunset: Permanent by design — same as the computedStyle gap; retire only if the policy is reversed.

screenshot.reason: The whole layout differs (7 stacked blocks vs Chrome's mixed inline/block flow with centering and list padding), so non-text pixels massively exceed the <=1% band. Intentional by design.
screenshot.sunset: Permanent by design — same as the computedStyle gap; retire only if the policy is reversed.
